en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, East Millstone, Somerset County, New Jersey, January 1911, Sheet 1

sheet-1.description: The single sheet of the January 1911 Sanborn atlas of East Millstone, a village of about 600 people in Franklin Township, Somerset County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It covers the village between the Delaware and Raritan Canal on the west and Franklin Street on the east, and from Amwell Road in the north to Elm Avenue in the south. Market Street runs north and south along the canal side, with William and Franklin Streets parallel to it; Livingstone Avenue crosses all three in the middle of the sheet. The canal runs down the left edge with a basin opening off it, a bridge carrying the road west over the canal, and a street lettered Canal along its east bank. Along Market Street are the village's shops and services: a post office, bakery, barber, tobacco and confectionery store, meat market and sausage factory, feed mill, farm implements and fertilizer store, a hay press, wagon shed and grain storage, the Franklin Hotel and the R.R. Hotel. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Millstone Branch crosses the sheet diagonally from the south-west, with its depot at Market Street and an engine house near William Street. The largest works is the Harmer Rubber Reclaiming Works on the canal at the south-west corner, drawn in detail with its reclaiming, drying, vulcanizing and scrap rubber buildings, a 10,000 gallon water tank and its own fire equipment. The rest is mainly frame dwellings on long lots. The Dutch Reformed Church stands at the top right and the M.E. Church below Elm Avenue at the bottom. The sheet carries its own key in the top left corner and the Sanborn title seal at the top right.
notes: Livingstone Avenue is Livingston Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Elm Avenue is Elm Street.
Market, William and Franklin are lettered without a suffix; they are Market Street, William Street and Franklin Street today.
The Pennsylvania Railroad Millstone Branch is abandoned; modern Bradley Avenue crosses Market and William Streets close to where the line ran.
Amwell Road meets Market Street in a wide open fork at the north end of block 2; OpenStreetMap has two nodes there 56 m apart, so that junction was not used as control.
Harmer Rubber Reclaiming Works at the south-west corner, with a watchman, hydrants and a small steam fire engine drawing from the canal.
Title seal: population 600; prevailing winds west; water facilities canals, wells and cisterns; no steam and no hand engine, no hose carts, no hook and ladder truck.

Single map sheet of the whole village, 50 ft to an inch, north towards the upper left (rotation about -28 degrees); own key top left, title seal top right. Streets: Amwell Rd, Market, William, Franklin, Livingstone Av (Livingston Avenue), Elm Av (Elm Street), Canal; D&R Canal and basin on the west, PRR Millstone Branch (abandoned) diagonally. One part.
